name: EFM8BB10F8I-A-SOIC16
title: EFM8BB1 Busy Bee family: 8-bit 8051 microcontrollers, 25 MHz, up to 8 kB flash, 12-bit ADC, SOIC16, QSOP24 and QFN20
summary: A small 8-bit microcontroller on the pipelined CIP-51 core (8051 instruction set) at up to 25 MHz, with up to 8 kB of flash and 512 bytes of RAM. It carries a 12-bit 200 ksps ADC with internal reference and temperature sensor, two low-current comparators, a 3-channel PCA for PWM, four 16-bit timers, a watchdog, UART, SPI, SMBus/I2C and a CRC unit, all routed to pins through a crossbar. It runs from one 2.2 V to 3.6 V supply with an internal 24.5 MHz oscillator and comes with a UART bootloader. EFM8BB10F8I-A-SOIC16 is the 8 kB, -40 to +125 °C part in SOIC16 with 13 I/O pins.
key_figures: 8 kB / 512 bytes (256 B RAM + 256 B XRAM); 4 kB and 2 kB versions
4.45 mA typ at 24.5 MHz; 105 µA typ in stop; 0.2 µA typ in shutdown

Grades: G is -40 to +85 °C; I is -40 to +125 °C; A is -40 to +125 °C with full automotive production status (AEC-Q100, IMDS registration and PPAP documentation). Every member of the family is AEC-Q100 qualified.
G and I grades come in QSOP24, SOIC16 and QFN20; the A grade comes only in QFN20.

Common to every part number: CIP-51 core up to 25 MHz, 24.5 MHz and 80 kHz internal oscillators, SMBus/I2C, SPI, UART, a 3-channel PCA, four 16-bit timers, two analog comparators, a 12-bit ADC with input multiplexer, voltage reference and temperature sensor, a 16-bit CRC unit and a factory UART bootloader.

operation.text: The CPU is the pipelined CIP-51, which runs the standard 8051 instruction set; about 70 % of instructions finish in one or two clocks, and the clock may go up to 25 MHz. The 8 kB parts carry 8 kB of flash that firmware can rewrite in system, and 512 bytes of RAM: the 256-byte 8051 internal RAM plus 256 bytes of XRAM. The 2 kB parts have 256 bytes of RAM.

Everything runs from the one VDD pin. The I/O drivers take their supply from VDD (these parts have no separate VIO pin) and most internal logic from an on-chip 1.8 V LDO. Each analog block can be turned off or set to low power, and the clocks of idle digital peripherals are gated off so they draw little.

Four modes. Normal: everything clocked. Idle: the core stops while peripherals keep running, and any interrupt resumes code. Stop: all internal power nets go down, the pins keep their state, and any reset source brings the part back. Shutdown: as Stop with the LDO also off; only the RSTb pin or a power-on reset wakes it. Stop and Shutdown are chosen by STOPCF in REG0CN before STOP in PCON0 is set.

Port pins P0.0 to P1.7 can each be a GPIO, an analog input, or a digital peripheral signal placed by the priority crossbar decoder; P2.0 and P2.1 are GPIO only, and C2D shares P2.0. Each port has two drive strength settings. INT0 and INT1 have their own vectors and can come from any of the P0 pins; up to 16 pins can raise the shared Port Match interrupt. All I/O pins are 5 V tolerant when the part is powered. Drive is 5 mA sourced and 12.5 mA sunk, enough for an LED.

Sources: the 24.5 MHz HFOSC0 (within ±2 % over supply and temperature), the 80 kHz LFOSC0, and a CMOS clock into EXTCLK (P0.3). The chosen source passes through a divider of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128. Out of reset the system clock is HFOSC0 divided by 8.

The programmable counter array has one 16-bit time base with a selectable clock and divider, and three capture/compare channels, each with its own CEXn pin through the crossbar. Channel modes: edge capture (rising, falling or both), internal-compare timer, high-speed toggle output, square-wave frequency output, and PWM of 8, 9, 10, 11 or 16 bits, edge or centre aligned, with polarity control. Comparator 0 can act as a hardware kill input.

Timer 0 and Timer 1 are the classic 8051 timers: clock from SYSCLK, SYSCLK/12, /4 or /48, EXTCLK/8, or a pin; modes are 13-bit, 16-bit and 8-bit auto-reload, and Timer 0 can split into two 8-bit timers. Timer 2 and Timer 3 are 16-bit auto-reload timers that can also split into two 8-bit auto-reload halves, clocked from SYSCLK, SYSCLK/12 or EXTCLK/8; Timer 2 can capture a pin, Timer 3 can capture LFOSC0.

Clocked by LFOSC0, the watchdog resets the MCU on overflow unless firmware restarts it in time. After every reset it is on, set to its longest interval. Firmware may disable it, or lock it on so that nothing can change it until the next reset. A watchdog reset leaves the RST pin alone.

UART0 is full duplex and supplies 8051 UART modes 1 and 3, with 8- or 9-bit data and automatic start and stop bits. Baud rates reach SYSCLK/2 for sending and SYSCLK/8 for receiving. A one-byte buffer each way lets a second byte start arriving before the first has been read.

SPI0 runs as master or slave, 3-wire or 4-wire, in all four clock phase and polarity settings, with several masters allowed on one bus. NSS can be a slave select input, a mode-fault input that stops a master when another master drives the bus, a chip-select output under firmware control, or unused. The clock reaches SYSCLK/2 as master and SYSCLK/10 as slave; an 8-bit generator sets the rate.

SMB0 follows SMBus 1.1 and works with I2C at 100 kbit/s and 400 kbit/s. It does master, slave and multi-master with hardware arbitration and synchronization, clock stretching, hardware recognition of 7-bit and general-call addresses (10-bit addresses in firmware), adjustable data setup and hold, and can ignore all slave traffic.

CRC0 computes the CCITT-16 polynomial 0x1021 over bytes written to it, with optional bit reversal per byte and a starting value of 0x0000 or 0xFFFF. It can also check flash by itself over one or more 256-byte blocks, taking 11 µs per block at 24.5 MHz.

ADC0 is a SAR converter with 12-, 10- and 8-bit modes, track-and-hold, a window comparator and up to 16 external inputs through its multiplexer (12 on the SOIC16). Rates reach 200 ksps at 12 bits and 800 ksps at 10 bits; slower low-power modes exist. Conversions start from software, a pin (CNVSTR) or a timer. Burst mode returns one accumulated result per start, with programmable power-up settling and tracking. Reference: internal at 1.65 V or 2.4 V, or external; the temperature sensor is an input.

CMP0 and CMP1 each pick a positive and a negative input from up to eight pins, or from the LDO output or GND. Hysteresis from 0 to ±20 mV, response time and supply current are programmable. Synchronous and asynchronous outputs can go to pins through the crossbar, and an interrupt can be raised on a rising edge, a falling edge or either.

Reset sources: power-on, the RSTb pin, comparator, software, the VDD supply monitor, the watchdog, the missing-clock detector and a flash error. In reset the core stops, registers return to their defaults (some bits only on power-on), port latches go to 1 in open-drain with weak pull-ups on, and interrupts and timers are off. RAM keeps its contents while power lasts. For power-on and supply-monitor resets the part holds RSTb low until it leaves reset. Code then starts at 0x0000 on the internal oscillator with the watchdog running.

The two-wire C2 interface (clock on C2CK, bidirectional data on C2D) programs flash and debugs the fitted part without using any of its resources, at full speed: memory and register access, four hardware breakpoints, single step, run and halt. All peripherals keep working while halted under debug.

The series resistors of the debug connection are needed only when RSTb or the P2.0 pin also goes to other circuits, such as a reset switch with a debounce filter. When neither does, the resistors and their adapter links can be omitted.

Every part ships with a UART bootloader in the code security page, the last 512-byte flash page (0x1E00 to 0x1FFF on 8 kB parts); it can be erased. Address 0x1FFF is the lock byte and 0x1FFE, just below it, the bootloader signature byte: 0xA5 there marks a bootloader as present, and then every reset jumps to the bootloader vector, which decides between staying in bootload mode and going to the reset vector at 0x0000. Any other value sends resets straight to 0x0000. The bootloader talks on TX = P0.4 and RX = P0.5; bootload mode is entered with P2.0/C2D on all three packages. Flash on 8 kB parts is 16 pages of 512 bytes.

The supply monitor trips between 1.85 V and 2.1 V, and the core, logic, flash and RAM are guaranteed down to its minimum. The VDD ramp time to 2.2 V is 10 µs minimum. Code starts 3 ms to 31 ms after VDD passes the power-on threshold. A low pulse of at least 15 µs on RST resets the part.

SOIC16 and QSOP24 are marked on three lines: EFM8; the part number designation followed by the revision letter; a trace code followed by the two-digit year and two-digit work week of assembly. QFN20 carries the part number designation on two lines, the trace code, then year, work week and revision.
